title: Strategic onboarding: technical + legal handshake
next_steps: Redwood to share redline-friendly MSA and DPA diff by 2026-05-21
SE to run brief throughput/latency benchmark on Helios sample workload (p95 target) by 2026-05-25
Pricing team to send committed usage/discount template by 2026-05-22
action_items: Ava Martinez - Send annotated MSA/DPA with clear note on KMS/HSM options - due 2026-05-21
Daniel Cho - Run 10k request perf test with Helios sample prompts + provide results and recommended quantization profile - due 2026-05-25
Marcus Lee - Provide sample data residency and egress requirements (EU sites, VPC peering) - due 2026-05-21
Rosa Alvarez - Flag any non-starter DPA clauses and confirm minimum audit evidence (SOC2 + encryption attestation) - due 2026-05-24
header:
Date: 2026-05-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 mins
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood CSM), Priya Singh (Helios Proc), Ethan Mallory (Helios CISO), Rosa Alvarez (Helios Legal), Marcus Lee (Helios Eng), Jin Park (Helios Product)
summary: Kickoff between Redwood and Helios to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations for Dedicated vs Private deployments, KMS/HSM keying options, data residency and pricing banding for an initial pilot. Key asks: Helios needs on-prem-ish control for PHI-inferred signals, strong audit/KMS controls, predictable p95 latency under 150 ms for short chat flows, and clarity on rollback/fallback policies. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send redline-friendly docs and SE to run benchmark on Helios prompts; pricing follow-up to formalize pilot commit and discount tier.
topics: Pricing for pilot and committed capacity
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: All right everyone, thanks for joining, this is Ava from Redwood. We wanted to do a combined legal + technical handshake so we can map next steps and surface any non-starters early.
[00:18] Priya Singh: Hi Ava, thanks. On our side we have procurement, legal, security and platform. We only have about 45 minutes for the procurement chunk but we can go deeper on the technical afterwards.
[00:30] Daniel Cho: Hi team, Daniel here, I'll handle the performance and deployment details. Quick ask — does Helios have any hard data residency or encryption constraints beyond PHI handling?
[00:40] Ethan Mallory: Yes, CISO here. PHI is the main one, and we're required to keep derived signals and logs within EU region for EU patient flows. We also want customer-managed keys via KMS or HSM, not vendor-managed if possible.
[00:55] Rosa Alvarez: Legal side: we'll go through MSA redlines after procurement gives the go — primary DPA questions are about subprocessors, breach notification windows, and data deletion semantics. We also need audit evidence: SOC 2 plus a statement about encryption-at-rest and in-transit.
[01:12] Ava Martinez: Totally understood. For KMS we support several models — customer-managed keys in cloud KMS, Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) with HSM providers, and in some Private deployments we can support a customer-side KMS gateway. We'll include options in the DPA.
[01:30] Marcus Lee: Marcus - from platform: what does the network topology look like for Private? We prefer VPC peering into a dedicated cluster or an on-prem package depending on throughput.
[01:40] Daniel Cho: For Redwood Dedicated we can provision a GPU pool in Helios' chosen region, and we support VPC peering with Allowlist and private egress. Private (on-prem) is heavier but available — it's basically a self-managed runtime with Redwood control plane optionally remote. Throughput numbers differ; Dedicated gives faster ramp and easier SLA.
[02:00] Jin Park: Quick pricing question: is there a lower tier for pilot? We're small team but need predictable spend.
[02:07] Ava Martinez: Absolutely — we usually do a 3-month pilot with committed minimum and a pilot discount. Pricing will be a table: per-token hosted vs per-hour dedicated GPU rate. We'll send a template after this call.
[02:20] Priya Singh: On the MSA, two high level asks: 1) limit subprocessors and 2) faster breach notification — 24 hours. Are those usually acceptable?
[02:31] Ava Martinez: Subprocessors are disclosed in the DPA appendix and we can accept a narrower subprocessors clause for enterprise deals; 24-hour breach notification is aggressive but we can commit to detection and initial notification within 24 hours, final root cause as we have it. We'll mark that in our redline.
[02:48] Rosa Alvarez: Also need indemnity carveouts around data re-identification.
[02:53] Ava Martinez: We'll have legal flag examples and propose a balanced indemnity clause.
[03:00] [brief cross-talk]
[03:15] Daniel Cho: On perf: what are your target p95 and token sizes? That will drive kernel/quantization choices.
[03:22] Marcus Lee: Typical chat flows are median 30 tokens response, worst-case 150 tokens. We need p95 under 150 ms for short flows, p95 under 300 ms for the 150 token case.
[03:37] Daniel Cho: That's a tough but achievable target for Dedicated with batching tuned for low-latency. For Private on-prem we'll have more deterministic latencies but need to confirm GPU specs. We'll run a synthetic with your prompts.
[03:50] Ethan Mallory: Also need KV cache persistence guarantees — if we cache prefixes, we need assurance on how it's stored and rotated, and if it's considered PHI.
[04:02] Daniel Cho: Great point. We treat KV cache as ephemeral in typical setups but for cache persistence options we encrypt at rest and can route it through customer KMS. We'll document the lifecycle in the DPA appendix.
[04:20] Priya Singh: About rollback and fallback — we need a policy if a model is rolled to a lower-cost variant; we can't have unpredictable quality regressions mid-run.
[04:30] Ava Martinez: We have rollout controls: canary percent, automatic fallback to a pinned previous model on regressions, and monitoring hooks to alert you. We can add explicit SLOs around quality regression windows.
[04:45] Rosa Alvarez: Regarding data deletion: we need a clear definition of deletion (logical vs physical) and an SLA for deletion after contract end.
[04:55] Ava Martinez: Standard is logical deletion within 30 days, and we can provide an option for certified physical deletion on private deployments with an attestation. We'll include those options.
[05:10] Marcus Lee: Network egress charges are a concern — if we peer into Dedicated we want predictable egress pricing or included in the committed tier.
[05:20] Ava Martinez: Pricing can include bundled egress in a committed SKU, we'll have the pricing team map that to your expected call volume.
[05:30] Jin Park: For the pilot we'd like to test both Dedicated and a small Private run to compare the p95 and ops overhead — is that feasible in parallel?
[05:38] Daniel Cho: Yes, but resource intensive. We usually do an initial Dedicated pilot and follow with Private if more control is required. We can carve out a short Private POC on premises if you can provide hardware specs.
[05:52] Priya Singh: Timebox — procurement wants a 3 week commercial decision post-pilot. Legal wants 2 weeks for review after we get redlines. Are those timelines aligned with Redwood's ramp?
[06:04] Ava Martinez: Yes, that's reasonable. We'll aim to deliver redline-ready MSA/DPA in 48 hours and then have the SE benchmark by week end. Pricing doc will be the same cadence.
[06:14] Rosa Alvarez: If you can provide a change-tracked MSA and a DPA with a subprocessor list and KMS options that will speed our review.
[06:24] Ava Martinez: Noted. We'll send a tracked MSA + DPA + an architecture note for the Private option.
[06:30] [short pause]
[06:45] Daniel Cho: Quick technical detail I want to confirm: do you expect inference to touch raw PHI or only derived metadata?
[06:52] Ethan Mallory: Both. We ingest raw clinical notes for summarization and generate derived patient signals. So the entire pipeline must be covered by the DPA and encryption at rest and in transit.
[07:05] Daniel Cho: Understood — that'll affect our container isolation and disk encryption defaults. We'll ensure the Private option has isolated node pools and encrypted ephemeral storage; Dedicated will have tenancy isolation and customer KMS options.
[07:22] Priya Singh: Do you provide audit logs with token-level tracing or only higher-level request logs? We need token-level for certain compliance cases.
[07:33] Liam O'Neill: We can provide detailed request-level audit trails, though token-level logging might be considered PII/PHI so it's off by default. We can support a mode where you route logs to your own log endpoint and retain them under your control.
[07:50] Rosa Alvarez: We might request that during an audit window.
[07:55] Ava Martinez: That's fine — we'll include a runbook for audit windows and log export procedures.
[08:05] Marcus Lee: On the perf benchmark, what's the expected deliverable? Latency percentiles, flops, GPU utilization?
[08:12] Daniel Cho: We'll deliver p50/p90/p95 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), GPU utilization and recommended quantization/kv cache settings. We'll also map recommended batch sizes and expected cost per 1M tokens.
[08:26] Jin Park: Is there a way to throttle model complexity per route? For example, lightweight embeddings for search vs full chat for triage.
[08:35] Daniel Cho: Yes, route-based model selection is supported. You can pin endpoints to different model families and the smart router will pick based on policy.
[08:45] Priya Singh: Another procurement ask: can the contract have an exit clause if performance or cost deviates by X percent?
[08:54] Ava Martinez: We can negotiate an SLA credit structure tied to p95 latency and uptime, and include a termination option for chronic regresses after remediation windows. We'll propose thresholds in the MSA appendix.
[09:08] Rosa Alvarez: We'll also need clarity on encryption key escrow and access during subpoenas — who handles that?
[09:16] Ava Martinez: If you use customer-managed keys, Redwood won't have the plaintext key; subpoenas go through your org. For Hosted, we can support key escrow options with an HSM partner if required. We'll document the flow.
[09:31] [sound of chair moving]
[09:40] Priya Singh: Okay, let's recap — Redwood to send MSA/DPA redlines and architecture note in 48 hours; SE to run perf tests on Helios sample prompts and deliver metrics by 2026-05-25; Pricing to send pilot pricing; Helios will provide sample prompts and egress/residency requirements by 2026-05-21. Anything else?
[09:58] Marcus Lee: I'll add hardware spec for Private if we go that route.
[10:02] Ava Martinez: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with a calendar invite for a benchmark review and post the artifacts in the shared Drive.
[10:12] Rosa Alvarez: One last legal note — please label the DPA appendix that covers PHI explicitly, that'll speed internal sign-off.
[10:20] Ava Martinez: Will do. Thanks all.
[10:25] [call ends]
